subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as a first-run onboarding/auth method, and what security, billing, account-detection, fallback, and documentation contract should it have?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing to present Anthropic OAuth as one-click onboarding crosses product UX, provider policy, and credential-security boundaries that automation cannot decide.

options.title: Add Additive OAuth After Approval
options.body: Expose a provider-owned Anthropic OAuth method only after maintainer-approved security, billing, docs, fallback, and live-provider proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Auth Paths
options.body: Keep API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI as the supported Anthropic paths and improve wording or docs instead of adding browser OAuth now.

options.title: Prototype Experimental OAuth
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth path that does not replace current Anthropic setup choices until proof and policy are strong.

recommendation.title: Add Additive OAuth After Approval
recommendation.body: Expose a provider-owned Anthropic OAuth method only after maintainer-approved security, billing, docs, fallback, and live-provider proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on the Anthropic onboarding/auth-choice paths closest to this request.
